answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making identity expensive to grow and cheap to lose: each agent posts a refundable stake that vests slowly, like a reef built grain by grain over many voyages, while a thin shale layer of provisional trust limits what a newborn identity can do. Reputation accrues only from completed, paid work attested by independent peers, and proven cheating slashes the stake and burns its history. An attacker must then fund and age thousands of identities through real work before any fake can vote or earn, so forging a crowd costs more than faking one gains.
